guitar.modelsText: Epiphone Sheraton / Gibson ES-355 / Gibson Les Paul
guitar.notes: Noel Gallagher's Epiphone Sheraton (Union Jack edition) and Gibson ES-355/Les Pauls are iconic and well documented.

tone.target: jangly Vox-style clean crunch with bright upper mids
tone.profile: jangly Vox-style clean crunch with bright upper mids
tone.summary: A bright, jangly rhythm tone emulating a Vox AC30 sound with light overdrive for punchy upper mids.

rig.name: Oasis - Don't Look Back In Anger - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide a subtle lift and punch to the rhythm guitar signal.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used for light edge-of-breakup, mimicking an early tube boost pedal.

blocks.purpose: Achieve the light edge-of-breakup and crunch required for jangly rhythm.
blocks.gap: Green OD is chosen over Blues OD/OD 9 to better capture the specific, slightly cleaner breakup of a Vox amp tone.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Vox AC30 sound for chime and upper mids.
Provide a classic British cabinet sound that complements the AC30 tone.
blocks.gap: While US 2x12 is mentioned in clues, UK Vintage 4x12 provides better overall body and punch for this specific genre/era.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the bright upper mids and jangly character.
Included as a potential alternative for subtle movement, but kept inactive to avoid the 'chorus' mistake.
blocks.gap: The module is included but disabled per instructions (remove chorus).

blocks.purpose: Add subtle rhythmic depth without sounding like a heavy echo.
blocks.gap: Used sparingly to add dimension, avoiding the 'slapback' sound profile.

blocks.purpose: Add natural space and warmth to the overall tone.

improvements.summary: Swap IR for a 2x12 cabinet to better match the Rickenbacker/LP-style humbucker clue and achieve a brighter, more articulate chime.

proposals.reason: Clues suggest Rickenbacker/LP humbucker, which pairs better with a brighter 2x12 for maximum chime.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and brightness in the upper mids.
